heard: A dead star struck Earth from 20,000 light years away. Spacecraft detectors across our solar system were suddenly blinded in August 1998. NASA's Rossi satellite was flooded by an invisible pulsating gamma ray wave. The signal flashed every 5.16 seconds from a magnetar called SGR 1900 plus 14. Its magnetic field is trillions of times stronger than Earth's entire field. Spitzer captured a seven-light-year ring of glowing dust left behind. The blast was powerful enough to physically alter Earth's atmosphere.
